title: HR-GUI current workflow evidence - termination, FMLA, workers compensation

facts: The Terminations module ingests routed documents, termination reports and possible resignation/notice emails into reviewable local cases.
Employee identity and termination date must be resolved/verified before generation.

Default rules expect a general termination form matching 'Term Employment Form' or 'Termination of Employment' and track employee, supervisor and HR signature evidence; local rules can override defaults.
Generated messages are saved as .eml drafts and are never sent automatically.
The module explicitly states that the established termination writer remains authoritative for the active-roster move until equivalent safeguards are incorporated.
findings.authority_note: This is current implementation evidence, not proof that every default signature/form rule is approved HR policy.

facts: The FMLA module is currently a RoutedInboxModule stub with a planned case schema.
Its planned text currently includes 'Hours used vs 480 (12 wk rolling)' and 5-business-day/15-calendar-day reminders.
findings.conflict: Canonical RTEC process knowledge says the organization's FMLA 12-month measurement method is unresolved and source materials conflict among occurrence/first-day, calendar-year and rolling approaches. The stub's rolling-language must not be promoted into production logic until authority is resolved.
findings.action: Treat the planned rolling method as an implementation candidate requiring validation, not current policy.

facts: The WorkersComp module is currently a RoutedInboxModule stub.
Its planned schema includes injury/report dates, witnesses, FROI date, claim number, carrier, lost/restricted time, wage statement, RTW status and OSHA 300 recordability.
findings.authority_note: The stub does not identify or validate the current RTEC carrier/TPA, portal, owner or claim workflow.

controls: Do not infer policy authority from software defaults.
Block FMLA balance/year-method automation until the authoritative RTEC measurement method is documented.
Keep consequential termination processing review-gated and preserve the established authoritative roster writer until a tested replacement is explicitly approved.
